newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk management predicts no full output halt.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk management predicts no full output halt.

text.p: A spokesman for Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group said on Monday that he thought it was unlikely that workers at the group's flagship metals plant would stop production fully by striking.
"There is a preliminary supposition that they will not stop output fully," said Anatoly Komrakov. "I don't think they could even consider stopping output fully."

The main trade union representing workers at the flagship mining and metal processing plant said earlier on Monday that it had gone ahead with a proposal to strike, giving management 10 days to meet workers' demands over salary and holiday arrears.
"You can't just stop the furnaces," Komrakov said. "To stage a real, proper strike and do it the right way, you would have to stop things for several months -- and nobody will go that far."
He said that the United Trade Union's strike committee was due to discuss on Tuesday particulars of any strike in the Arctic town of Norilsk where the plant is situated.
"We will have their final decision tomorrow," Komrakov said.
A union official had said any strike would involve a minimum of 50,000 workers in mining and processing metals and a maximum of the plant's entire workforce of 120,000.
But Komrakov played down the possibility of action on such a scale, adding, "we have good workers at the plant who know it is not in their interests to undertake such action."
The Norilsk Nickel group owes 900 billion roubles ($160 million) in salary and holiday arrears and 1.2 trillion roubles ($211 million) to various budgets.
The group has a plan to pay off arrears by the end of this year but union officials have demanded swifter action.
Norilsk Nickel is a major supplier of nickel, cobalt and platinum group metals to world markets.
